messages:
Maria: heads up — ran a 72h long-context soak on canary and one of the GPUs hit an OOM at ~03:12UTC. stack trace points straight at kv cache growth + heavy paging; no obvious spike in incoming qps.
Kevin: ugh, which canary? r-inf-03?
Maria: yep r-inf-03. It slowly drifted up over ~30m then paged a bunch and finally OOMed. attaching a tiny excerpt of the allocator log below.
runtime-bot: uploaded logs to s3://redwood-infra/soak/r-inf-03/3945000000/ (link omitted)
Maria: log snippet:
```
[03:09:45] kv_alloc: resident=11.8GB, reserved=14.0GB
[03:10:12] kv_page: evict_rate=0.3/s, fragmentation=0.62
[03:11:30] kv_alloc: resident=13.9GB, reserved=14.0GB
[03:12:07] OOM: cannot allocate 256MB for KV slab
```
Dmitri: can you share the flamegraph? also, did kernel-selector flip to the alternate attention kernel during that window? sometimes that increases slab usage for int8 kernels.
Maria: flamegraph uploaded. kernel-selector did a fallback at 03:08 to kernel_v2 (the one with larger scratch allocations) for batches > 8 tokens. batching heuristics changed yesterday in canary (auto-batch tuning).
Ashley: so two correlated things: a kernel that needs more temporary KV-ish memory + batching that tends to produce larger per-request KV footprints. combined with slow eviction/fragmentation.
Kevin: do we have evidence the eviction path was starving? eviction rate=0.3/s seems low for that memory pressure. were compactions happening?
Maria: compaction attempts were queued but kept restarting due to page scan races — see repeated "compaction_aborted: lock contention" lines. fragmentation stayed ~0.6 for the last 20m.
Julian: interesting — we've seen fragmentation creep when many tiny prefixes are created and we never compact them because compaction is too expensive during spikes. is the workload here generating many ephemeral prefixes?
Maria: yes, the replay uses thousands of short-lived system messages that create many tiny cache entries; not typical customer workload but reproducer for long dialogs.
Dmitri: quick mitigation: canary a config that enables incremental compaction + limits per-prefix residency. two knobs: kv.compact_incremental=true and kv.prefix_max_resident=8MB.
Kevin: also consider short-circuiting to CPU decode on severe memory pressure — keep serving but with higher latency. that's graceful degradation we should have as a safety net.
Ashley: agreed. I'd rather degrade latency than lose requests. For now, can we config the canary to:
```
kv.compact_incremental=true
kv.prefix_max_resident=8MB
batcher.max_tokens=512
kv.soft_evict_threshold=0.85
```
and rerun the soak?
Maria: applied those on the canary at 03:30. re-running soak now.
runtime-bot: canary config change applied by Maria at 03:30; deployments: kernel-selector unchanged.
Julian: FYI we should add telemetry to correlate kernel-selection switches with kv_alloc deltas. propose a histogram: kv_alloc_delta_by_kernel{kernel_name}.
Dmitri: good idea. also add a sampling profiler for compaction tasks so we see how often they abort and why.
Kevin: next steps:
- Maria: run soak and capture 24h with new knobs (in progress)
- Dmitri + Julian: instrument kv_alloc_delta_by_kernel + compaction_abort_reasons (task)
- Ashley: design fallback path to CPU decode under kv OOMs (proposal by EOD)
- Ops: add alert when kv.fragmentation > 0.58 for >15m with resident > 10GB
Maria: I'll open infra ticket INF-1287 and attach logs/flamegraphs. If the incremental compaction stabilizes fragmentation, we can roll to more canaries.
Julian: small note — kernel-selection may still cause transient spikes even with prefix caps. we should also throttle large-batch auto-batching for long-context jobs (batcher.max_batch_tokens cap).
Ashley: agreed. once we have instrumentation, we can set an automated mitigation: on detection of kv growth + kernel flip, reduce max_batch_tokens and force kernel_v1.
Maria: soak is at +2h with new config — will report back if we still see drift. thanks all. :thumbsup:
